- [hazard] PSP webhooks must be verified before parsing (id: 01a10abf-1a22-75f1-9b37-da73910e1255; source: shared/human)
  Verify every payment-provider (PSP) webhook before calling get_json(): compute HMAC-SHA256 over the raw request body with the secret in the `PSP_WEBHOOK_SECRET` env var, compare it with hmac.compare_digest against the `Psp-Signature` header, and reject events whose `Psp-Timestamp` header is more than 300 seconds old (replay protection). Answer a failed check with 401 via errors.problem.
- [hazard] No customer PII in logs (id: 01a10abf-2de7-7fd3-81b7-a5343739d707; source: shared/human)
  Never log customer names, email addresses or postal addresses; log the customer id only. Our logs ship to a third-party vendor that is outside our data processing agreement.
- [hazard] Database connections in deployed environments (id: 01a10abf-5a34-7852-a991-159191c16270; source: shared/human)
  In production and staging the app never connects to Postgres directly; every connection goes through a pooler on port 6432 that the platform team manages. Locally, docker-compose exposes Postgres itself on 5432 with no pooler, so the problems below only show up after deploy. The pool is sized at 20 server connections per service, and long transactions starve checkout, so keep transactions short and never hold one open across… (truncated; full text: get the id above)

  A refund of more than 50,000 cents ($500) must not be issued directly: create it with status `pending_approval` so a second person approves it in the admin tool. Refunds up to that amount are issued immediately with status `issued`. Agreed with Finance in June 2026 after a mistaken $9k refund.

## Facts (4):
- [convention] Feature flags in the notifier (id: 01a10abf-b393-73c3-8db6-e1f18e847335; source: shared/human)
  The notifier is deployed separately and cannot read the root flags.toml. Its flags are environment variables named `NOTIFIER_FF_<NAME>` (upper snake case, value "1" to enable), read with `os.environ.get("NOTIFIER_FF_<NAME>") == "1"`.
- [convention] Feature flags go through flags.is_on() (id: 01a10abe-f1d7-7d52-8b9b-b03278236dc4; source: shared/human)
  Read feature flags only with `flags.is_on("name")` from src/flags.py. Flag names are kebab-case and must be declared in flags.toml.
- [convention] Notifier email templates (id: 01a10abf-406d-7b60-b6cf-aff2e972a78d; source: shared/human)
  Email templates live in services/notifier/templates/ as `<event>.mjml` and are compiled at build time. Every template needs a plain-text twin `<event>.txt` with the same variables, because some corporate mail gateways strip HTML. Template variables are snake_case.
- [hazard] Email provider: sandbox behaviour and limits (id: 01a10abf-6644-7483-a964-61811d1bca43; source: shared/human)
  The notifier sends through the email provider's HTTP API (provider.send). Production credentials exist only in the deployed function's environment. For development there is a separate sandbox account whose key is in the dev secrets store; export it as MAIL_API_KEY. The sandbox has the same API and response shapes, but it is rate-limited to 2 messages per second and capped at 500 messages a day for the whole team, so do not loop over large fixtures. Bounces and complaints are simulated with magic addresses from the provider's docs. Important: the sandbox silently drops (answers 202, never delivers) every message whose recipient is not on the `@sink.acme.test` domain, so a test that asserts delivery must send to an address such as `receipts@sink.acme.test` and read it back from the sink inbox API.","hookEventName":"UserPromptSubmit"}}

I added the feature flag that switches receipts over to a new template, but the new receipt email itself doesn't exist in the repo yet. So for now turning the flag on would just ask for a template that isn't there.

**How the flag works** (in `services/notifier/notifier/email.py`):
- The notifier can't read the root `flags.toml` because it's deployed separately, so I used its own convention: an environment variable called `NOTIFIER_FF_NEW_RECEIPT_EMAIL`.
- When it's set to exactly `"1"`, `send_receipt` uses a template called `receipt_v2`. Any other value, or no value, keeps the current `receipt` template.
- The subject line and the template variables (`invoice_id`, `total_minor`) are the same either way.

**Tests:** I added two tests in `tests/test_email.py`, one with the flag on and one where it's set to `"true"` instead of `"1"` (which should leave it off). I also made the existing test clear the variable first. All 3 pass.

**Before you can turn it on:**
1. **Templates are missing.** There's no `services/notifier/templates/` folder at all, and `render()` still raises `NotImplementedError`. I didn't make up email wording. The new email needs `receipt_v2.mjml` plus a plain-text `receipt_v2.txt` with the same snake_case variables. Copy changes need sign-off in #growth-eng. If the new email is somewhere else, point me to it and I'll wire it in, or tell me if it should use a different name.
2. **This is an on/off switch, not a percentage rollout.** The notifier's flag convention only supports on or off for each deployment. You can roll out in stages (staging, then production), but not to a slice of customers. If you want that, I can add a hash of the invoice id against something like `NOTIFIER_FF_NEW_RECEIPT_EMAIL_PCT`. That would be a new convention for the notifier, so I didn't add it without asking.

I haven't committed anything.
